extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected and created multimodal questions based on their expertise, adhering to copyright and license regulations. Quality control involved three stages: 1) identifying potential duplicates using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, 2) distributing problems among co-authors for format and typo checking, and 3) categorizing problems into four difficulty levels and excluding overly simplistic ones.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including the paper's co-authors, who specialize in the majors/subjects covered by the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases introduced during the manual curation process.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited by potential biases from manual curation and its focus on college-level subjects, which may not be entirely sufficient for comprehensively testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark helps monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which has significant societal implications including potential job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as a benchmark to evaluate multimodal models. It is split into a few-shot development set, a validation set for hyperparameter selection, and a test set.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was partitioned into specific splits: a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning and filtering involved removing duplicate problems based on lexical overlap and URL similarity, standardizing formatting, correcting typos, and excluding overly simplistic questions.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks... MMMU , constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: MMMU, constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
